body_text: Gut health is an essential aspect of overall health and well-being, as the gut plays a key role in digestion, immunity, and even mental health. Unfortunately, many people struggle with poor gut health, which can lead to a range of issues such as bloating, constipation, diarrhea, and even more serious conditions like inflammatory bowel disease. If you're looking to improve your gut health, here are some tips to get you started: Eat a variety of fiber-rich foods: Fiber is essential for good gut health, as it helps to keep things moving through the digestive system and promotes the growth of healthy bacteria in the gut. Aim to include plenty of fiber-rich foods in your diet, such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes. Stay hydrated: Drinking plenty of water is important for overall health, but it's especially important for the gut. Water helps to keep the digestive system moving and prevents constipation. Aim for at least 8 cups of water per day. Eat fermented foods: Fermented foods, such as yogurt, kefir, and sauerkraut, contain beneficial bacteria that can help to improve gut health. Adding these foods to your diet can help to balance the bacteria in your gut and promote a healthy digestive system. Limit processed and sugary foods: Processed and sugary foods can disrupt the balance of bacteria in the gut and contribute to digestive problems. Limiting your intake of these types of foods can help to improve gut health. Get enough sleep: Sleep is essential for overall health, and it's also important for gut health. Lack of sleep can disrupt the balance of bacteria in the gut and lead to digestive problems. Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep per night. Manage stress: Chronic stress can disrupt the balance of bacteria in the gut and lead to digestive problems. Finding ways to manage stress, such as through meditation, yoga, or exercise, can help to improve gut health. Exercise regularly: Exercise can help to improve digestion and promote the growth of healthy bacteria in the gut. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate exercise per day. In summary, there are several simple ways to improve gut health. Incorporating fiber-rich foods, staying hydrated, eating fermented foods, limiting processed and sugary foods, getting enough sleep, managing stress, and exercising regularly can all help to promote a healthy digestive system and overall well-being. By making these lifestyle changes, you can take steps towards improving your gut health and enjoying better overall health.

title: Why React Native is the Future of Mobile App Development
summary: Why React Native leads mobile app development with native performance, shared codebases, and strong community support.
body_text: As the world becomes increasingly reliant on mobile technology, the demand for high-quality mobile apps continues to grow. As a result, businesses and developers alike are constantly searching for the most effective and efficient ways to build these apps. React Native is a popular open-source mobile app framework that allows developers to build native mobile apps using the same design as React. In short, React Native allows developers to create truly native mobile apps using the same design principles and codebase as web apps built with React. But why is React Native considered the future of mobile app development? Here are just a few reasons: Enhanced Performance In addition to offering an improved user experience, React Native also offers enhanced performance. Because React Native apps are built using native code, they are able to leverage the full power of the device’s hardware and operating system. This means that React Native apps are faster, smoother, and more responsive than traditional hybrid apps. Shared Codebase Another major advantage of React Native is the ability to share code between web and mobile apps. This means that developers can reuse their existing codebase and design principles, reducing the time and effort required to build and maintain multiple versions of an app. This also allows for easier collaboration between teams and a more consistent user experience across platforms. Strong Community Support React Native is an open-source framework, which means that it has a strong and supportive community of developers behind it. This community is constantly contributing to the framework, adding new features and capabilities and providing support and guidance to other developers. This level of support is invaluable for businesses and developers looking to adopt React Native. Versatility and Flexibility Finally, React Native is incredibly versatile and flexible. It can be used to build a wide range of mobile apps, from simple utilities to complex, data-intensive apps. It also offers a wide range of customization options, allowing developers to tailor their apps to the specific needs and preferences of their users. React Native is the future of mobile app development because it offers improved user experience, enhanced performance, a shared codebase, strong community support, and versatility and flexibility. title: Most popular AI apps in 2022
summary: How did AI make our lives easier in 2022? Here are the most popular AI apps grouped by category.
body_text: 2022 was a breakthrough year in AI We learned that Generative AI has a massive impact on everything from creative industries to business operations. Millions of people are actively using AI tools today which shows that our society is ready to welcome AI into their daily lives. Gartner [estimates]( https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press- releases/2022-10-10-gartner-identifies-seven-technology-disruptions-that-will- impact-sales-through-2027) that by 2025 Generative AI will account for 10% of all data produced, and for 30% of all outbound marketing messages from large brands. In this blog post, we will cover some of the most popular apps in 2022 to help you prepare for 2023, which is certainly going to be another pivotal year for AI. This overview will cover applications in the following fields of Generative AI: Text Video Image Code Speech Music Text It’s not just businesses that can benefit from text creation with Generative AI in the form of chatbots or copywriting tools. Anyone can use it to create essays, creative stories, character descriptions, translations, and much more. GPT-3 This large language model from OpenAI can generate human-like text. You can use it for many things, like letting it suggest slogans or simply asking it about certain topics. It is very general-purpose text generation. GPT-3 OpenAI playground Try it out: beta.openai.com ChatGPT ChatGPT is a fine-tuned version of a model in the GPT-3.5 series. You can read more about its use cases and limitations here . The purpose of ChatGPT is to be used in a conversational manner. However, do bear in mind that most answers are very long and quite generic. ChatGPT chat window Try it out: chat.openai.com/chat Quickchat AI This brings us to Quickchat AI. You can think of it as a conversational layer built on top of large language models like GPT-3. It allows you to customize them for a business use case by adding your own Personality , Knowledge Base and Integrations . Read more about the specifics of the possible customizations and use cases [here]( https://quickchat.ai/post/chat-gpt in-businesses/). Quickchat AI - Settings Quickchat AI - Knowledge Base Try it out: app.quickchat.ai Emerson AI Emerson is a multilingual AI conversation partner . You can use it to learn new things, study languages or just to chat, Emerson does have a sense of humor for sure. You can use the Emerson AI mobile app to talk to Emerson via texting or voice & audio. If you are using Telegram , Emerson will respond to photos you send it. Emerson AI - voice & audio conversation Emerson responding to photos on Telegram Try it out: quickchat.ai/emerson Copy.ai Copywriting tools like copy.ai are perfect for creating text more efficiently. You can write basically anything, from social media posts to blogs to wedding vows. If you need a translation, you can create your text in over 25 languages. Copywriting with copy.ai Try it out: copy.ai Video Synthesia Whether you need a training or marketing video, this video creation platform lets you create personalized videos in minutes. Just enter your text and choose between different AI avatars and AI voices. Synthesia’s video creator tool Try it out: synthesia.io Runway ML Runway ML revolutionizes video editing, offering a variety of AI Magic Tools ranging from background removal, motion tracking, transcript creation, color grading a video with text, and much more. You can even add a green background to your video in seconds - it seems like green screens will be obsolete in the future. A few months ago, Runway announced that a text-to-video feature would be coming soon, allowing you to edit videos by typing commands. Runway ML video editor Try it out: runwayml.com Image With the various text-to-image generators that have hit the market this year, anyone can create their own AI art. There are also many useful apps using AI for enhancing photos or images as well as transforming existing images by removing or adding objects. Lensa This photo editor for selfies and photo retouching features a smart eraser and many pro adjustments. Lensa AI can also create Magic Avatars from selfies you feed it. Lensa app Try it out: prisma-ai.com/lensa Vizcom Vizcom develops creative tools for artists and designers. It can help you create optimized 3D renders of your drawings in seconds which can save you an enormous amount of time. Vizcom creative tool Try it out: vizcom.ai Stable Diffusion AI art has taken the internet by the storm this summer. With text-to-image models like Stable Diffusion, you can easily create pictures by entering a text prompt (like we did for the image in our [recent blog post]( https://quickchat.ai/post/create-ai-bot-for-whatsapp bot/) on how to build conversational AI on WhatsApp). Oh, and be sure to add a negative prompt, telling the Stable Diffusion model what you don’t want to have in the image. Image has been generated with Stable Diffusion 2.1 using the following prompt: Futuristic robot announcing WhatsApp integration, beautiful colourful artistic photograph Try it out: huggingface.co/spaces/stabilityai/stable- diffusion Code AI is becoming an increasingly important tool for software developers, increasing efficiency and accuracy. It can not only speed up the coding process, but also fully automate it. GitHub Copilot The AI pair programmer helps you write code faster and with less work. It draws context from comments and code and suggests lines and functions. A few weeks ago, a new brush feature was released to help you fix bugs and make your code cleaner and more robust. GitHub Copilot in use Try it out: github.com/features/copilot ChatGPT While GitHub Copilot helps you with coding, ChatGPT can generate code from scratch. Just tell it what you want to code, and it will do the job. It can also find bugs in your code. ChatGPT - coding example Try it out: chat.openai.com/chat Speech Speech synthesis is the artificial production of human speech, allowing you to create voice-overs in a click. It is becoming increasingly popular and you’ve probably heard AI voices in social media videos, ads, call centers or smart assistants in the last month. Resemble.ai With this voice generation tool, you can create human-like voice recordings in different languages. You can integrate custom voices into your favorite tools and even clone your own voice by recording samples. (Pro tip from my first- hand experience: use a good microphone). resemble.ai voice generation tool Try it out: resemble.ai Podcast.ai Did you know that there is a podcast that is generated entirely by artificial intelligence? But of course, if you have no idea how to create beats, AI can generate music from scratch. Mubert Mubert generates music tracks in an instant. summary: Cleaning out your closet doesn’t have to be confusing or stressful! Like looking through old photos or meeting up with a past friend, a closet clean-out can be a chance to reflect on how you’ve changed and where you’re headed. By taking the time to ask yourself four simple questions, you can be one step […]
body_text: Cleaning out your closet doesn’t have to be confusing or stressful! Like looking through old photos or meeting up with a past friend, a closet clean-out can be a chance to reflect on how you’ve changed and where you’re headed. By taking the time to ask yourself four simple questions, you can be one step closer to having a thrifted wardrobe that changes with your lifestyle ♻️. 1. How does this fit me? Try to dig a little deeper beyond how the piece fits your body – when you wear it, do you feel comfortable and confident? Try on some clothes in the mirror, turn on your favorite music, and take note of how the color, texture, and movement of the piece makes you feel. If you’re sure you’d want to resell a piece on Curtsy, you can use this time to start creating content for Try-On videos ! Create a yes, no, and maybe pile, and remember that they aren’t set in stone. Pieces can be moved around as you keep asking yourself these questions. 2. How does this fit my lifestyle? What do you spend a majority of your time doing for work, me-time, and social time? If you work from home, you’ll need comfy yet professional basics. To make getting out of the house on weekends that much more exciting, you might want some extra glam dresses ( Revolve dresses are my go-to 💛). If you’re on a sports team at school, maybe you could use some North Face pieces that keep you cozy on walks to class and activewear that fits just right. 3. Can I give this more life or am I ready to let go? Sometimes you’ll come across pieces you’ve had for so long you can’t imagine letting them go, like a leather jacket that’s been with you through years of ups and downs. Think about the care the item requires and if you have the time/energy to fix any damage. If it’ll just be taking up space after many closet cleanouts, it could feel refreshing to resell that pre-loved item to someone new! Even better if the category or brand is trending on Curtsy and could sell super quickly 🤑! 4. How can I expand on styles outside of my comfort zone? The best part about a closet clean-out is that it helps your closet evolve with you 🌱. Are there any pieces that stuck out to you that you’ve been nervous to wear, but want to try, like vintage sweaters ? Or a piece you thought was your aesthetic but no longer feels right (that might even still have the tags on 🏷️)? Reselling is the perfect way to explore looks outside of your comfort zone while knowing you’re sustainably switching pieces in and out. Ready to clear out the old and bring in the (like)-new? title: Deep Cleaning 101: How to Effectively Clean Out Your Refrigerator
summary: A clean refrigerator is essential for maintaining good hygiene and preventing the spread of germs and bacteria. In this blog post, we will share some tips on how to effectively cle
body_text: A clean refrigerator is essential for maintaining good hygiene and preventing the spread of germs and bacteria. However, cleaning a refrigerator can often be a daunting task, especially when it comes to tackling tough stains and removing spoiled food. In this blog post, we will share some tips on how to effectively clean out your refrigerator and keep it looking and smelling fresh and clean. Step 1: Empty the refrigerator. Before you begin cleaning, remove all the food, drinks, and condiments from the refrigerator. This will make it easier for you to clean and also give you the opportunity to check for expired or spoiled food and dispose of it. Step 2: Clean the shelves and drawers. Use a mixture of warm water and mild dish soap to wash the shelves and drawers. Scrub away any stains or spills, paying special attention to corners and crevices. Rinse with clean water and dry with a clean cloth. Step 3: Clean the door seals. The door seals are often overlooked when cleaning, but they can accumulate a lot of dirt and grime. Use a mixture of warm water and mild dish soap to wash the door seals, then wipe them down with a clean, damp cloth. Step 4: Clean the interior. Use a mixture of warm water and mild dish soap to wash the interior of the refrigerator, including the walls, ceiling, and floor. Scrub away any stains or spills, and pay special attention to the corners and crevices. Rinse with clean water and dry with a clean cloth. Step 5: Clean the exterior. Use a mixture of warm water and mild dish soap to wash the exterior of the refrigerator, including the handles and the control panel. Wipe down with a clean, damp cloth. Step 6: Clean the coils. The coils are located at the back or bottom of the refrigerator and they can accumulate dust and dirt, which can make your refrigerator less energy efficient and shorten its lifespan. To clean the coils, unplug the refrigerator and use a brush or a vacuum cleaner to remove dirt and debris. Step 7: Organize the food. Once your refrigerator is clean, put the food, drinks and condiments back in, making sure to organize them in a way that makes it easy for you to see what you have and find what you need. By following these steps, you can effectively clean your refrigerator and keep it looking and smelling fresh and clean. Remember to always unplug the refrigerator before cleaning and to use the appropriate cleaning products and tools to ensure that the refrigerator is thoroughly cleaned. In conclusion, cleaning your refrigerator may seem like a daunting task, but by following these tips and using the right tools and techniques, you can easily tackle tough stains and spoiled food. By keeping your refrigerator clean, you can maintain good hygiene, improve the air quality, and extend the life of your appliance.

title: Muay Thai vs Kickboxing: What's the Difference?
summary: FightCamp is breaking down the history and techniques behind two powerhouse martial art forms. Learn the differences between Muay Thai and Kickboxing.
body_text: Is Muay Thai Kickboxing? At first glance, Muay Thai and Kickboxing can look indistinguishable. Both Muay Thai and Kickboxing employ a stand-up fighting style (as opposed to grappling-based martial art forms like wrestling or Brazilian Jiu Jitsu). When it comes to competition, both operate on a 3-5 round timed structure on a platform or in a ring. And though both stem from the same ancient weaponless combat form, the two martial arts are actually very distinct. In this blog, we’ll demystify the difference between Kickboxing and Muay Thai and the history of both combat sports. Muay Thai vs Kickboxing: History The History of Muay Thai Often called “the art of 8 limbs,” Muay Thai traces its roots back to ancient Thailand—or Siam. The martial art was born out of unarmed military combat training and has evolved over the years to become one of the most popular styles of martial arts across the globe. Muay Thai gained popularity in the western hemisphere around the time of World War I and adopted several western boxing practices, such as padded boxing gloves and 3-5 timed rounds in a ring. Bangkok continues to be revered as the premier city for training in traditional Muay Thai. The History of Kickboxing In its purest form, American Kickboxing is a hybrid martial art developed in mid-1900s Japan by fighters who adapted Karate, Western boxing, and Muay Thai techniques. The term “Kickboxing” was first coined by Osamu Noguchi, who wanted to create a sport where Karate and Muay Thai fighters could compete against each other. The Karate influence can especially be seen in the Kickboxer’s bladed stance and snappy, knee-hinging kicks. The new sport quickly gained popularity across Thailand and was later brought to the Netherlands by a Dutch martial artist named Jan Plas. Plas developed Dutch Kickboxing with an emphasis on high-volume punches, forward pressure, and hard low kicks. American Kickboxing quickly distinguished itself by trading in the point-fighting system for full contact combat. American Kickboxing also prohibits low kicks to the thigh or calf. Muay Thai vs. Kickboxing: 5 Key Differences Striking Systems - Kickboxing is built on a 4-point striking system (2 punches and 2 kicks), while Muay Thai uses an 8-point striking system that includes knee strikes, elbow strikes, and upper body grappling that’s referred to as the “full clinch.” Because of this, Kickboxers often fight from a distance, while Muay Thai artists move in and out of their opponent’s pocket. Movement - Thai fighters tend to move at a more even pace—their foundational footwork movement is a forward 1-2-3 march called the Yang Sam Khum that keeps their feet flat-footed and their head centerline. In contrast, Kickboxers stay on the balls of their feet and bounce and circle around the ring. Kickboxers move in and out of the striker zone at a lightning-fast pace, cutting angles with their footwork to set up and doge attacks. Stance - If a Muay Thai fighter and a Kickboxer are facing each other in a ring (say, in a UFC or Bellator Mixed Martial Arts fight), they’re going to hold their bodies very differently. The Muay Thai fighter will be standing flat on their feet, hips facing their opponent, hands at their temples to block strikes. The Kickboxer will be bouncing on their feet with one foot significantly ahead of the other, creating a bladed stance that turns the side of their torso towards their opponent. Their hands will likely be a little lower, as Kickboxers fight from a distance. Kicks - Kicks to the body and head are cornerstones of both Muay Thai and Kickboxing…but not all kicks are created equal. In Muay Thai, fighters kick by turning their hips and landing with the lower shin. They don’t bend their knee, but rather keep the leg relaxed until the moment of impact, resulting in a powerhouse of a kick that can feel and sound like the crack of a baseball bat. It’s because of this force that Muay Thai artists are trained to check their opponent’s kicks to prevent serious damage to their legs. Kickboxers, on the other hand, hinge from the knee and lift the leg up to strike with the foot rather than the shin. Because pure kickboxing fights are often scored by points, fighters are motivated to deliver rapid-fire kicks that may not knock out their opponent but will rack up points for strikes. In American Kickboxing, fighters are not allowed to throw kicks to their opponent’s thighs or calves. Volume and Pace - Watch even just one round of Kickboxing and you’ll be able to grasp how much of kickboxing is a barrage of strikes. Kickboxers are volume strikers—they strike fast and often, punctuating strike combos with a mix of high and low kicks. On the other hand, Muay Thai fighters tend to fight with a more patient and measured style. Many Muay Thai gyms coach a Sabai Sabai mindset, which loosely translates to “keep it chill.” The idea is to slowly wear down your opponent and then when they’re tired, knock them out with ruthless efficiency. At the end of the day, both Muay Thai and Kickboxing are incredible workouts, great for your mental health, and badass as hell. So now that you know what's the difference between Kickboxing and Muay Thai are you ready to try them? title: CNC Milling Machine: Processes and Operations
summary: Learn more about the CNC milling process and methods.
body_text: What are the Types of CNC Milling Operations? The types of CNC Milling operations are listed below. Face Milling: In face milling, the cutter axis is perpendicular to the machined surface, and material removal occurs mainly through cutting edges on the face and periphery of the cutter. Multiple cutting edges remove material across a wide area in a single pass. Face milling produces smooth finishes on large planar sections (machine bases, mounting plates). Peripheral Milling: Peripheral milling removes material using the cutter’s outer circumference while the cutter axis is parallel to the machined surface. The cutting tool rotates parallel to the machined surface during material removal. Peripheral milling shapes profiles, steps, and side walls with controlled depth. Slot Milling: Slot milling typically uses an end mill or slotting cutter that may plunge or ramp into the material and then move along the slot path. The cutter removes material between two parallel walls with precise width control. Slot milling supports keyways, channels, and internal tracks (guide rails, fastener paths). Drilling: The drilling produces round holes by feeding a rotating drill bit into the workpiece. The spindle controls depth and diameter through programmed coordinates. Drilling operations maintain alignment and positional accuracy for fastening or assembly. Contour Milling: The contour milling forms complex shapes through coordinated multi-axis movement. The cutter follows curved or irregular toolpaths defined by digital programming. Contour milling typically produces curved surfaces or complex profiles by following programmed toolpaths, and may involve multi-axis machining for 3D geometries, belonging to the types of CNC milling operations . How are Different Milling Operations Performed? Different milling operations are performed by selecting specific cutting tools and defining precise tool paths within the control program. The machining process begins with choosing the appropriate cutter (face mill, end mill, slot drill, twist drill) based on the required geometry and surface finish. Tool geometry determines cutting edge contact, chip evacuation, and material removal rate during each operation. Feed rate and spindle speed are adjusted according to material type (aluminum, steel, titanium) and cutter diameter to maintain stable cutting conditions. Programming controls depth of cut, axis movement, and cutting direction through structured G-code commands. Linear and circular interpolation guide the tool along programmed coordinates to produce flat faces, slots, holes, or contoured surfaces. Depth increments are defined to prevent excessive load on the spindle and reduce tool deflection. Cutting direction (climb milling, conventional milling) influences surface finish and tool wear patterns. Automated tool changes support sequential operations within one machining cycle to complete complex components efficiently. Precision control of parameters ensures dimensional accuracy and repeatability in a CNC Milling Machine. Is Face Milling Used for Flat Surfaces? Yes, face milling is used to create flat surfaces on a workpiece. In face milling, the cutter axis is perpendicular to the machined surface, and cutting occurs primarily at the face and periphery of the cutter. Relative motion between the tool and workpiece produces the cut; depending on machine design, either the table, spindle, or both may move. Multiple cutting inserts mounted on the face of the cutter remove material across a broad area during each pass. The wide cutting diameter allows efficient surface coverage and uniform material removal. Face milling produces smooth and level finishes by distributing cutting forces evenly across the tool path. Controlled spindle speed and feed rate maintain consistent chip formation and reduce surface irregularities. Rigid machine structure minimizes vibration that affects flatness and parallelism. Machining parameters define depth of cut and overlap between passes to achieve precise surface tolerances (±0.01 mm in standard industrial applications). Manufacturing operations rely on face milling to prepare base plates, mounting surfaces, and structural components before further machining inside a CNC Milling Machine. How does CNC Milling Compare to Laser Cutting? CNC milling and laser cutting are different manufacturing processes with distinct capabilities; milling is suited for 3D machining and thick materials, while laser cutting is optimized for high-speed cutting of thin sheets and profiles. CNC milling removes material mechanically through rotating cutters that shape a workpiece into the desired form. The process involves precise control of the cutting tool's speed, depth, and path, which allows for the creation of complex geometries, including three-dimensional shapes. CNC milling is particularly effective for handling thicker materials (up to several inches) and achieving tight tolerances. It is commonly used for parts like engine blocks, molds, and detailed structural components. Laser cutting utilizes a focused laser beam to melt, burn, or vaporize material, cutting through thinner sheets with high precision. Laser cutting can cut moderately thick materials (often up to ~20–30 mm steel with high-power industrial lasers), though cutting speed and efficiency decrease as thickness increases, while it excels in speed and accuracy for cutting profiles from thin metal or plastic sheets. CNC milling can achieve more intricate features in 3D space, such as pockets, slots, and complex contours, making it suitable for a wider range of applications. Laser cutting, on the other hand, is often faster and more efficient when it comes to cutting thin profiles in materials. Both processes have their specific strengths, with Laser Cutting offering speed in thin sheet processing and CNC milling being preferred for more complex, three-dimensional parts. When Should You Use CNC Milling Instead of Laser Cutting? You should use CNC milling when parts require depth, contours, or 3D features instead of laser cutting. CNC milling excels at creating intricate shapes with precise depth control and complex geometries. It is the preferred method for machining thicker materials, such as metals, plastics, and composites, that laser cutting may not effectively handle. CNC milling is ideal for components with complex internal features like pockets, slots, and threads, which require mechanical cutting. CNC milling can achieve high dimensional accuracy for 3D features, while laser cutting provides excellent accuracy for 2D profile cutting, but cannot produce 3D features or deep cavities. The ability to perform multiple cutting operations, including drilling, shaping, and engraving, in one setup makes CNC milling versatile for manufacturing complex components. Laser cutting, while faster for thin sheet profiles, lacks the capability to produce intricate 3D shapes or handle high material thicknesses. CNC milling is essential for industries requiring precision and complex geometries, such as aerospace, automotive, and medical device manufacturing. Does Milling Produce a Better Surface Finish Than Grinding? No, milling does not produce a better surface finish than grinding. Grinding uses abrasive wheels that can achieve very low surface roughness and high dimensional accuracy, though the final precision also depends on machine rigidity, wheel condition, and process parameters. It is particularly effective for achieving smooth, fine finishes on hard materials and components with tight tolerances. Grinding operations are designed to deliver superior surface quality, often used in processes requiring high finish standards, such as in automotive or aerospace manufacturing. Milling, on the other hand, is mainly for shaping materials and performing moderate finishing operations. While CNC milling can achieve good surface finishes, it does not match the precision or smoothness that grinding offers. Milling involves mechanical cutting, which is effective for producing complex shapes and detailed features, but it leaves a slightly rougher surface compared to the fine abrasive action of grinding. Grinding remains the preferred method over milling for parts that require a high-quality finish. What are the Types of Machining Processes? The types of machining processes are listed below. Milling: Uses a rotating cutter to remove material from a workpiece. The cutter moves along multiple axes to shape flat or complex surfaces. CNC milling machines control the movement and cutting parameters for precise and intricate parts. Turning: Involves rotating the workpiece while a stationary cutting tool removes material. The process is ideal for producing cylindrical shapes, such as shafts, spindles, and bearings. The cutting tool moves along the workpiece's surface to create the desired diameter and finish. Drilling: Produces round holes by feeding a rotating drill bit into the material. This process is essential for creating holes of various sizes and depths. Drilling operations can be performed with high precision, and the depth and diameter can be controlled through CNC programming. Grinding: An abrasive finishing process that uses rotating wheels to remove small amounts of material from the surface. It is used to achieve smooth finishes and tight tolerances on hard materials. Grinding improves the surface quality and can be used to sharpen or refine parts. EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining): EDM removes material through controlled electrical discharges (sparks) between an electrode and a conductive workpiece submerged in dielectric fluid. It is useful for hard or complex materials that are difficult to machine with traditional cutting methods. The process provides high precision and is commonly used in toolmaking and die manufacturing for various types of machining processes . How Does CNC Milling Compare to Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM)? CNC milling cuts material mechanically using rotating tools, while Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) removes material through the controlled application of electrical sparks. A rotating cutter moves across the workpiece, removing material layer by layer to create desired shapes and features in CNC milling. Milling is faster for general machining tasks (surface finishing, contouring, and producing complex 2D shapes). EDM is effective for machining very hard materials (hardened steel or exotic alloys) that are difficult to cut using traditional methods. EDM excels in creating intricate cavities, fine details, and small, complex features that are difficult to achieve with CNC milling. The process is ideal for producing parts with narrow slots, deep holes, or sharp internal corners in tool and die manufacturing. Its ability to produce highly accurate, delicate shapes makes it indispensable for certain applications, although EDM is slower compared to CNC milling. The Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) remains the preferred choice for precision in machining hard materials and fine cavities. Is CNC Machining More Accurate than Manual Machining? Yes, CNC machining is more accurate than manual machining. CNC machines are controlled by computer programs that execute precise movements, which significantly reduces the potential for human error. The CNC machines follow pre-programmed instructions, ensuring exact movements and tool changes, unlike manual machining, where the operator manually adjusts the machine settings and tool positions. CNC machining ensures consistent repeatability by automating the entire process. CNC machines can produce highly repeatable parts across production runs, though variation can still occur due to tool wear, thermal effects, machine calibration, and fixturing conditions. The precision of CNC machining allows for accuracies within ±0.005 mm, compared to the limitations of manual machining, where factors like operator fatigue, tool wear, and slight adjustments can introduce errors. The ability to replicate complex designs without deviation makes CNC machining the preferred method for producing high-precision parts in industries such as aerospace, automotive, and medical device manufacturing. What Materials are Used in CNC Milling? The materials used in CNC milling are listed below. Aluminum: Lightweight, easy to machine, and has good thermal conductivity. It is commonly used for parts that require strength-to-weight ratios, such as in the automotive and aerospace industries. Its soft nature makes it ideal for quick, efficient cutting. Steel: Steel is strong, durable, and highly versatile, making it suitable for a wide range of applications, from structural components to high-strength mechanical parts. Some steels have high wear resistance (especially tool steels and hardened alloys), while many common steels, such as mild steel metal , prioritize strength and ductility rather than wear resistance. Stainless Steel: Corrosion-resistant and maintains strength in high-temperature environments. It is commonly used in industries that require durability and resistance to rust, such as medical devices, food processing, and marine applications. Brass: Offers good machinability, strength, and corrosion resistance, making it ideal for intricate parts. It is commonly used in electrical components, fittings, and decorative items due to its attractive appearance and ease of shaping. Plastics: Lightweight and used for components where weight is a concern, such as enclosures or prototypes. Plastics such as ABS, PVC, and nylon are commonly machined for prototypes, low-to-medium production, or specialized components, while high-volume production is often achieved through injection molding rather than CNC machining. How do Material Properties Affect Machining Performance? Material properties affect machining performance by influencing cutting speed, tool wear, and overall machining efficiency. The hardness of a material is one of the primary factors, as harder materials require slower cutting speeds and increase the stress on cutting tools, leading to faster tool wear. Materials like hardened steel or titanium exert more force on the cutting edges, reducing tool life and requiring more frequent replacements or maintenance. Ductile materials (aluminum and brass) are easier to cut as they absorb more energy before breaking, resulting in smoother finishes and higher cutting speeds. Stainless steel has lower thermal conductivity than many metals (e.g., aluminum), which can lead to heat concentration near the cutting zone and increased tool wear. It causes workpiece distortion or affects the tool's ability to maintain precision. Proper tool selection, cutting speeds, and cooling methods help mitigate challenges posed by material properties, ensuring efficient and effective machining processes. Are Superalloys Difficult to Machine? Yes, superalloys are difficult to machine. Superalloys are designed to resist high temperatures and deformation, which makes them ideal for extreme conditions but challenging for machining. Superalloy’s exceptional strength and resistance to heat cause rapid tool wear, requiring more frequent tool changes. Machining speeds are slower compared to softer materials like aluminum or steel. The high hardness and toughness of superalloys make them resistant to traditional cutting methods, leading to higher forces on the tools and generating significant heat. Heat generated during machining can accelerate tool wear and affect dimensional stability, particularly due to localized temperature buildup and workpiece distortion. Specialized tools and advanced cooling methods, such as high-pressure coolant systems, are employed to counter these challenges. The measures help reduce tool wear and maintain cutting efficiency while working with superalloy material . Is Stainless Steel Harder to Machine Than Aluminum? Yes, stainless steel is harder to machine than aluminum. Stainless steel has higher strength and lower thermal conductivity, which makes it more resistant to cutting forces and generates more heat during machining. The increased heat leads to greater tool wear, requiring slower cutting speeds and more frequent tool replacements. Aluminum is softer, easier to cut, and dissipates heat more effectively, allowing for faster machining speeds with less strain on the tools. Aluminum's lower strength makes it more forgiving when it comes to machining, leading to improved surface finishes and more efficient production cycles. The combination of the properties makes aluminum a more suitable choice for high-speed and high-volume machining, whereas stainless steel presents more challenges due to its toughness and heat resistance. What are the Advantages of CNC Milling? The advantages of CNC milling are listed below. High Accuracy: High-precision CNC milling systems can achieve tolerances around ±0.005 mm under controlled conditions, while typical industrial machining tolerances are often ±0.01–±0.05 mm depending on machine capability, tooling, and setup. The precise control of tool position and speed ensures that parts are produced with high dimensional accuracy. Repeatability: CNC milling enables consistent mass production, with each part being identical. Automated processes ensure uniformity, reducing the potential for human error in large-scale production runs. Complex Geometry: Multi-axis CNC milling allows for the creation of intricate designs (curved or irregular shapes) that are difficult or impossible with traditional machining methods. Automation: CNC milling reduces the need for manual labor by automating processes, minimizing human error, and improving efficiency. It leads to more consistent results with less direct human involvement. How Can CNC Milling Reduce Production Costs? CNC milling reduces production costs through automation and precision. The automated nature of CNC milling allows for quicker setup times and fewer errors, minimizing the need for costly rework. Precision machining ensures that parts meet specifications on the first pass, reducing scrap material and waste. The cost of production is lower with reduced manual labor and more efficient use of materials. Efficient programming optimizes cycle time, allowing machines to run faster while maintaining quality. CNC machines operate for extended hours, reducing labor costs and speeding up the production process. The combination of automation, improved precision, and efficient use of materials results in cost-effective manufacturing, making CNC milling a preferred choice for industries that require high-volume production. Does CNC Milling Improve Dimensional Accuracy? Yes, CNC milling improves dimensional accuracy. Digital control systems precisely direct the machine's movements, ensuring consistent and accurate positioning of the cutting tool. The systems allow for controlled cutting speeds, tool paths, and depth, resulting in parts with high accuracy. The repeatable motion of CNC machines reduces variation between parts, even in long production runs. Proper calibration of the machine and regular maintenance further ensure that tolerances remain tight, minimizing the chances of errors over time. The precision is important for applications where high-quality parts are required, such as in aerospace and medical device manufacturing. What are the Limitations of CNC Milling? The limitations of CNC milling are listed below. High Initial Cost : CNC milling machines range widely in price, from tens of thousands of dollars for small 3-axis machines to several hundred thousand dollars or more for advanced multi-axis industrial systems. Specialized tooling and maintenance contribute to ongoing costs. Material Waste : CNC milling removes material from a larger workpiece, resulting in material waste. The efficiency of material usage is affected by the complexity of the part being produced. Tool Wear : CNC milling tools experience wear over time when machining hard materials. Regular maintenance and tool replacements are necessary to ensure optimal machine performance. Programming Skill : CNC machining requires programming knowledge or CAM software expertise, though modern workflows often separate roles between CNC programmers, CAM engineers, and machine operators. Inadequate programming or mistakes in the code lead to errors, defective parts, and increased rework. What Factors Affect CNC Milling Tolerances? The factors that affect CNC tolerances are machine rigidity, tooling, fixturing, thermal stability, machine calibration, cutting parameters, and material properties. The rigidity of the machine frame and the stability of the tool holder play significant roles in maintaining precise motion and reducing deformation during the cutting process. Thermal expansion and vibrations during machining influence the final dimensions of the part. Thermal expansion of the machine structure, spindle, tooling, and workpiece can cause dimensional variation during machining. Proper calibration and temperature control help minimize the effects and ensure tighter tolerances. Selecting the right tooling for the material and regularly maintaining the machine contribute to achieving the required precision in CNC milling. Is CNC Milling Suitable for Large Complex Parts? Yes, CNC milling is suitable for large, complex parts. Multi-axis CNC milling machines handle intricate geometries, allowing for the machining of parts with complex shapes and detailed features. The machines manipulate the tool and workpiece along several axes, enabling the creation of deep pockets, holes, and curved surfaces with high precision. The size and rigidity of the CNC machine play a key role in determining its capacity for larger parts. A larger machine with a more robust frame can accommodate bigger workpieces while maintaining accuracy during machining. Machine rigidity minimizes vibrations and deflections, ensuring that even large parts retain their dimensional integrity. CNC milling is commonly used for large aerospace, automotive, and industrial components, where size and complexity are critical. How do you Maintain a CNC Milling Machine? Maintaining a CNC milling machine involves several steps to ensure optimal performance and accuracy. First, regularly clean the machine and its components to prevent debris buildup, which leads to poor machining results and excessive wear. Second, lubricate moving parts, including ball screws, guideways, and spindles, to minimize friction and ensure smooth operation. Third, Calibration typically involves checking machine positioning accuracy, backlash, and geometric alignment using precision measurement tools, rather than simple axis alignment checks alone. Lastly, inspect cutting tools for wear and replace them when necessary to maintain machining precision. Regular maintenance helps reduce downtime, extends the life of the machine, and ensures consistent production quality. What are Common CNC Milling Defects? The common CNC milling defects are listed below. Burrs: Sharp edges left after cutting, due to improper tool settings or cutting speeds. The edges affect part quality and require additional deburring processes. Chatter Marks: Surface vibrations caused by machine instability or improper feed rates, leading to irregular patterns on the material surface. Dimensional Errors: Occur when parts do not meet specified measurements, due to machine calibration issues or tool wear. Tool Marks: Visible traces left on the workpiece surface, caused by worn or improperly selected tools that fail to produce a smooth finish. Can Proper Maintenance Prevent Milling Errors? Yes, proper maintenance reduces the likelihood of milling errors and improves machining stability, but it does not completely eliminate defects. Well-maintained components reduce backlash and vibration, which are common causes of inaccuracies during machining. Regular cleaning, lubrication, and inspection of machine parts help maintain smooth operation and minimize the risk of defects like dimensional errors and tool marks. Regular calibration ensures that all machine axes are properly aligned and that tools are set to the correct offsets. Proper maintenance improves machining consistency, extending the lifespan of the machine and tools. Maintenance ensures that parts meet tight tolerances and high-quality standards, reducing the need for rework or scrap by addressing potential issues before they affect production.

title: Supabase Wrappers, a Postgres FDW framework written in Rust
summary: A framework for building Postgres Foreign Data Wrappers which connects to Stripe, Firebase, Clickhouse, and more.
body_text: Today we're releasing Supabase Wrappers , a framework for building Postgres Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW) which connects Postgres to external systems. Foreign Data Wrappers are a core feature of PostgreSQL. We've extended this feature to query other databases or any other external system (including third-party APIs), using SQL. We're releasing Wrappers today in Alpha, with support for Firebase and Stripe . Wrappers for Clickhouse, BigQuery, and Airtable are under development. Example with Stripe # Let's step through a full example using the Stripe Wrapper. Connecting to Stripe # First, let's give your Postgres database some authentication details to access your Stripe account: _10 create server stripe_server _10 foreign data wrapper stripe_wrapper _10 options (api_key 'sk_test_xxx'); Creating a Foreign Table # Now we can map your Stripe data to Foreign Tables, which are just like normal tables except that the data exists outside of your database. _10 -- Create a foreign table for your Stripe products _10 create foreign table products ( _10 id text, _10 name text, _10 description text, _10 default_price text _10 ) _10 server my_stripe_server _10 options ( object 'products' ); Accessing remote data # After setting up your foreign table, you can query you Stripe products directly from your database: _10 -- Fetch all your stripe products in Postgres _10 select * _10 from products _10 limit 10; Or from your application, using one of our client libraries: _11 import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js' _11 _11 const SUPABASE_URL = 'https://xyzcompany.supabase.co' _11 const SUPABASE_KEY = 'public-anon-key' _11 _11 const supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_KEY) _11 _11 const { data: stripeCustomers, error } = supabase _11 .from('products') _11 .select('id, name, description, default_price') _11 .limit(10) Note: we kept this example simple, however for API security and code organization, you should store your foreign data in a separate schema . Use cases # Once we've added more Wrappers, they enable various possibilities: On-demand Big Data: Query your Data Warehouse on demand using Wrappers for Clickhouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Oracle, and S3. Simplified Onboarding: Migrate to Postgres from systems like Firebase, Microsoft SQL Server, and Airtable. Simplified Development: Create a new Stripe customer object within a Postgres function. AI capabilities: Run AI queries from your database using OpenAI's API. Caching: use Postgres triggers to insert data into in-memory databases like Redis. SRE and DevOps: Query your infrastructure state, like AWS and DNS records. Web3 Apps: integrate with IPFS and blockchains like Ethereum. Financial Apps: Build Financial applications using wrappers around Finance APIs. Community analytics: Analyze your community engagement with GitHub, Slack, Discord, and Twitter wrappers. On-demand ETL # In their 2017 paper , researchers from the University of Bologna investigated an approach to on-demand ETL: In traditional OLAP systems, the ETL process loads all available data in the data warehouse before users start querying them. In some cases, this may be either inconvenient (because data are supplied from a provider for a fee) or unfeasible (because of their size); on the other hand, directly launching each analysis query on source data would not enable data reuse, leading to poor performance and high costs. The alternative investigated in this paper is that of fetching and storing data on-demand. Their paper outlines the foundation for QETL (pronounced "kettle"): Query, Extract, Transform, Load. This differs from a more traditional ETL/ELT approach, where data is moved from one place to another. In QETL, the “Query” function allows data engineers to access data in a remote system even before moving it. This approach reduces the reliance on data engineering infrastructure, allowing teams to access operational insights faster. The benefits of QETL # We've built upon this concept using PostgreSQL's FDW system. This a new tool for developers and data engineers, with several benefits: Simplicity: the Wrappers API is just SQL, so data engineers don't need to learn new tools and languages. On-demand: analytical data is available within your product without any additional infrastructure, and the time it takes to retrieve that data is close to executing a query on the source. Always in sync: data which isn't moved will always be in sync. Developers can set up local views which re-map remote data into clean local schemas. Integrated: large datasets are available within your application, and can be joined with your operational/transactional data. Save on bandwidth: only extract/load what you need. Save on time: avoid setting up additional data pipelines. Save on Data Engineering costs: less infrastructure to be managed. QETL + Postgres # How does this look in action? Assuming that all of your analytical data is stored in Snowflake, you could create a foreign table inside your Supabase database: _10 create foreign table snowflake.order_history ( _10 id bigint, _10 ts timestamptz, _10 event text, _10 user_id uuid _10 ) _10 server my_snowflake_warehouse _10 options (table 'order_history', rowid_column 'id'); Now from your Supabase database you can query your Snowflake data directly: _10 select * from snowflake.order_history limit 1000; You can even join remote data with your local tables to enrich existing operational data. For example, to figure out how many times a user has purchased something from your store: _10 select _10 users.id, _10 count(order_history.event) _10 from _10 snowflake.order_history _10 join auth.users on auth.users.id = snowflake.order_history.user_id _10 where order_history.event = 'purchase' and order_history.user_id = '<some_user_id>'; We can either run these queries on demand or, for better query performance, we can run them in the background (using something like pg_cron ), and materialize the data into a local table. This gives us the basis of QETL: Query: run on-demand SQL queries, directly from your Postgres database. Extract: run SQL select statements on external systems, either on demand or on a recurring basis. Transform: use SQL aggregations and CTEs to transform the data. Load: store transformed data into local tables for faster access. This is a two-way process. It's equally useful to offload large datasets from your Postgres database to your Data Warehouse. With FDWs, this can be as simple as: _10 insert into snowflake.analytics _10 select * from analytics _10 where ts > (now() - interval '1 DAY'); On-demand ETL is a strong compliment for current ETL practices, and another tool in the toolbelt for Data Engineering and Developers that works with immediately with tools that interface with Postgres. Postgres, the everything interface # In a recent Software Engineering episode Andy Pavlo (database Professor at Carnegie Mellon and Co-Founder of OtterTune), explored the future between “better databases” and “better interfaces” [00:37:18]: Specialized engines are always going to outperform general-purpose ones. The question is whether the specialized engine is going to have such a significant difference in performance that it can overcome the limitations of a general purpose one. ... The challenge oftentimes is this: is the benefit you're getting from a specialized engine because the Engine is different or the API is different?. Andy Pavlo He goes on to explore the benefits of a Graph database vs a Relational database. Our recent release of pg_graphql closes the gap on the graph use-case by building a GraphQL API directly into Postgres as an extension. While a specialized graph database might provide performance benefits over Postgres, perhaps one of the largest benefits is simply the Graph API which makes it easier to reason about the data. With the introduction of Wrappers, we're hoping to close the gap on even more of these type of workloads. An exciting part of the FDW approach is that it provides a common interface to the world: SQL. While it has many shortcomings, SQL is the lingua franca of data. Postgres' FDWs transform any API into a data set with a common interface. This “interface aggregator” is similar to the promise of GraphQL engines. The benefit of embedding this functionality in the database is that it exists at the lowest level of the tech stack . Everything that is built on top can leverage it. While Postgres cannot easily access the functionality of a GraphQL server, a GraphQL server can easily access the functionality of Postgres. The FDW interface also future-proofs Postgres. Instead of keeping up with the latest technological advances, Postgres can instead act as an interface whenever they develop. The recent advance in AI and ML is a great example of this: AI technology is developing faster than the time it would take to build a new “AI database”. With a FDW, Postgres can become the interface to this technology and many other technological advances in the future. Developing Wrappers # Postgres has a builtin “Postgres FDW” allows querying one Postgres database from another. We've extended this functionality to support a variety of data sources, from Data Warehouses to APIs. This release includes two initial wrappers: Stripe and Firebase Integration Platform Self-hosted select insert update delete Firebase 🚧 ✅ ✅ 🚧 🚧 🚧 Postgres ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Stripe 🚧 ✅ ✅ 🚧 🚧 🚧 With several more under development : Integration select insert update delete Airtable ✅ 🚧 🚧 🚧 BigQuery ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ClickHouse ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Wrappers used pgx , extending it with FDW support. pgx is a Postgres extension framework written in Rust. Wrappers is very similar to Steampipe or Multicorn . We opted to develop our own framework for several reasons: The current state of FDWs is in disarray. It's hard to know which FDWs are supported and functional. We think there's a benefit to colocating all FDWs in a single repository using modern tooling. This makes contributing simpler and maintenance faster. Wrappers has async support, which enables the development of RESTful API-based FDWs, like Stripe. It's written in Rust, which provides reliable performance, strong typing, data security, and “push down” is supported through the framework. Supported types and Push Down # Wrappers supports a variety of types, including: bool , i8 , i16 , f32 , i32 , f64 , i64 , String , Date , Timestamp , and JsonB . Foreign Data Wrappers have a concept of "push down". This means that the FDW runs the query on remote data source. This is useful for performance reasons, as the remote data source can often perform the query more efficiently than Postgres. Push down is also useful for security reasons, as the remote data source can enforce access control. Limited push-down support has been added as a Proof of Concept, but this will be a key focus of Wrappers. You can follow development of all the Wrappers in the official GitHub Repo . Next Steps # We're not "officially" releasing Wrappers onto the platform yet, although the brave and curious might be able to figure out how to use it "unofficially". Caveat emptor: there will be breaking changes. We're excited to see what the community does with Wrappers. We're hoping that Wrappers will help to accelerate the adoption of Postgres as a data hub. If you're interested in getting involved or building your own Wrapper, don't hesitate to jump into the code and start developing with us. Star & Watch the GitHub repo: github.com/supabase/wrappers View the documentation: supabase.github.io/wrappers Supabase Launch Week: supabase.com/launch-week More Launch Week 6 # Day 1: New Supabase Docs, built with Next.js Day 2: Supabase Storage v2: Image resizing and Smart CDN Day 3: Multi-factor Authentication via Row Level Security Enforcement Day 5: Supabase Vault is now in Beta Community Day Point in Time Recovery is now available Custom Domain Names are now available Wrap Up: everything we shipped

title: This New Year, Ditch Resolutions and Nourish You Instead
summary: New Year, new me. Who doesn’t like the sound of that? For the average person, this can be exciting, yet for a [new] mama, it can be overwhelming. body_text: New Year, new me. Who doesn’t like the sound of that? For the average person, this can be exciting, yet for a [new] mama, it can be overwhelming. If you got caught up in the whirlwind of annual New Year’s resolutions, piling on affirmations and goals that you missed in the hullabaloo of 2022, then you know that next year’s resolutions look like a daunting to-do list that needs more than solutions to get through. That’s why we challenge you to dare to do things differently in the New Year. Choose calm instead of the chaos of trying to reach a perfection that doesn’t exist and focus on nourishing yourself. Whether that’s ditching the cringe New Year’s resolutions or adding a calming fave like our Lavender Bathtime collection to your daily self-care routine, it is time to do what is best for you. Maybe you would prefer our Gently Nourishing Collection that includes shampoo and face + body lotion that is gentle enough for you and baby? Whichever works, know that the journey to becoming the “best mother” is acknowledging that there is no such thing as a “best mother”. After all, what is motherhood but a personal journey that looks different for every lucky lady called to the chaos? Here are some other things to remind yourself about motherhood: 1. Perfection lies in your imperfections. In adult relationships, no one can connect with someone who tries to be perfect. It’s suffocating! In your quest to be the perfect mother (who does not exist), you alienate yourself from your precious baby and the village designed to support you in this chaotic quest. Give yourself grace, mama! What does grace look like? Baby’s bathtime schedule got thrown off because your Zoom call ran longer than expected? It’s okay. You let the screen babysit your feisty toddler for an hour while you finished some chores, although you swore your kid wouldn’t be a screen kid? Totally okay. You’re a human being, not a fictionalized super mom who can stretch herself in a thousand directions at once like Mrs. Incredible or something. 2. Be real with yourself and others, too. Before having your first baby, you have no clue what you’re doing. After a while, you hope to get in the swing of things but quickly realize that when it comes to raising babies, no two days are the same, and you never have all the answers! Lean into the unpredictability of motherhood and into your village even more. Like you, your village may have no clue what to do, but at least they’re there cheering on you and your little one every step of the way. This means if you are too tired to change a paw-printed diaper , let your spouse, mom, or whoever is with you know what you need. If you want someone to babysit for a few hours while you nap or step outside for fresh air, ask for help. Yes, the fear that you may not get the help you need when you need it is real. But the love that your village has for you is realer. Shoot your shot, mama. 3. Laugh, and cry, a little or a lot. Some say, “if you don’t laugh, you’ll cry.” Well, isn't crying cathartic? Crying releases oxytocin and endogenous opioids, feel-good chemicals that help ease emotional pain. As for laughter, we all know that a good laugh is the best form of medicine. When you miss your spa appointment for the umpteenth time, try our Me Time for Mama Daily Indulgence 10-piece set for new moms-to-be or Spa Time Anytime Luxury 10-piece set post-partum. If you still can't carve out time to indulge, laugh and cry a little or a lot. Whichever way, you will get the release you need and hopefully realize that the unscripted craziness of motherhood is ultimately worth it all! 4. Ditch the filter. We get it - motherhood has a way of getting in the way of your glamorous moments. Messy, disheveled buns replace sleek ponytails. Pink and pouty lips look a lot more like dry, chapped lips season in and out. And let’s not get started on eyeshadow for a casual but cute night out - do you even remember how to do a cut crease? While you may want to lament what feels like losses during motherhood, can we encourage you to look on the bright side? Makeup-free days mean your skin has more time to breathe. Cutting back on your beauty routine gives you the opportunity to focus on your day-to-night skincare routine. Never mind if it’s only three steps instead of your typical 12-step skincare routine. This looks like replacing your fave Honest foundation with Hydrogel Cream for dewy, brilliant skin even while the baby is having a complete meltdown. Or replace your eyeshadow with Depuff + C Eye Cream to help brighten the look of dark undereye circles and minimize the appearance of puffy eyes earned because the baby just can’t seem to sleep through the night. When you finally strike a selfie, you’ll be proud to show off your filter-free natural beauty. Now, how do these sound for New Year’s resolutions? Honestly doable? We think so! Remember: New Year, nourish you, always. How will You Prioritize Nourishing You in the New Year? Sources: 9 Benefits of Crying and Why it’s Good and When to Get Help.
